packet.headline_seed: Netflix trying to "poison regulators" about WBD merger, Paramount lawyer claims
packet.description_seed: Paramount Skydance is accusing Netflix of maintaining a campaign against its proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). In a June 5 letter (PDF) addressed to Jared A. Hughes, acting section chief of the Media, Entertainment, and Communications Section of the US Department of Justice's (DOJ's) Antitrust Division, and A. Maya Kahn, a trial attorney for the Antitrust Division, and first reported on by Politico today, Paramount chief legal officer Makan Delrahim accused Netflix of trying to influence stakeholders about the merger. The letter reads: Indeed, Netflix’s panic-level response and scorched-earth campaign to try and poison regulators and other stakeholders against the Transaction shows just how seriously Netflix takes Paramount as a scaled competitor. The letter from Delrahim, a former assistant attorney general for the Antitrust Division, is a response to a letter that The International Brotherhood of Teamsters sent to the DOJ in March. The teamsters' letter argued that Paramount and WBD's merger would threaten film and TV workers. The union, which has 1.3 million members, asked the DOJ to block the merger "unless substantial and enforceable safeguards are put in place to increase domestic production and protect jobs," per an announcement from the group. Paramount Skydance is accusing Netflix of maintaining a campaign against its proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). In a June 5 letter (PDF) addressed to Jared A. Hughes, acting section chief of the Media, Entertainment, and Communications Section of the US Department of Justice’s (DOJ’s) Antitrust Division, and A. Maya Kahn, a trial attorney for the Antitrust Division, and first reported on by Politico today, Paramount chief legal officer Makan Delrahim accused Netflix of trying to influence stakeholders about the merger. The letter reads: Indeed, Netflix’s panic-level response and scorched-earth campaign to try and poison regulators and other stakeholders against the Transaction shows just how seriously Netflix takes Paramount as a scaled competitor.

The letter from Delrahim, a former assistant attorney general for the Antitrust Division, is a response to a letter that The International Brotherhood of Teamsters sent to the DOJ in March. The teamsters’ letter argued that Paramount and WBD’s merger would threaten film and TV workers. The union, which has 1.3 million members, asked the DOJ to block the merger “unless substantial and enforceable safeguards are put in place to increase domestic production and protect jobs,” per an announcement from the group. Paramount’s top lawyer, however, this month argued that the merger would “not reduce work opportunities for the Teamsters or other organized labor” and would lead Paramount to create more content, including movies and programming for its streaming services and broadcast TV channels. This will push competitors to follow suit, Delrahim claimed.

"Netflix's panic-level response and scorched-earth campaign to try and poison regulators and other stakeholders against the Transaction shows just how seriously Netflix takes Paramount as a scaled competitor," Delrahim wrote in a June 5th letter to lawyers in the DOJ's Antitrust Division. Paramount claims that Netflix has been comparing the Paramount/Warner Bros deal with the 2019 merger between Disney and 21st Century Fox, and pushing how mergers such as these lead to a reduction in production and competition – and layoffs. "We understand that as part of its broader proxy war against the Transaction, Netflix has tried to persuade the Teamsters and other stakeholders that Disney's acquisition of Fox had a negative impact on content production and labor opportunities. Frankly, Netflix's 'sky is falling' narrative departs significantly from the ground-truth reality of what actually happened."

Paramount Skydance is accusing Netflix of maintaining a campaign against its proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD).

In a June 5 letter (PDF) addressed to Jared A. Hughes, acting section chief of the Media, Entertainment, and Communications Section of the US Department of Justice’s (DOJ’s) Antitrust Division, and A. Maya Kahn, a trial attorney for the Antitrust Division, and first reported on by Politico today, Paramount chief legal officer Makan Delrahim accused Netflix of trying to influence stakeholders about the merger. The letter reads:

Indeed, Netflix’s panic-level response and scorched-earth campaign to try and poison regulators and other stakeholders against the Transaction shows just how seriously Netflix takes Paramount as a scaled competitor.

The letter from Delrahim, a former assistant attorney general for the Antitrust Division, is a response to a letter that The International Brotherhood of Teamsters sent to the DOJ in March. The teamsters’ letter argued that Paramount and WBD’s merger would threaten film and TV workers. The union, which has 1.3 million members, asked the DOJ to block the merger “unless substantial and enforceable safeguards are put in place to increase domestic production and protect jobs,” per an announcement from the group.

Paramount’s top lawyer, however, this month argued that the merger would “not reduce work opportunities for the Teamsters or other organized labor” and would lead Paramount to create more content, including movies and programming for its streaming services and broadcast TV channels. This will push competitors to follow suit, Delrahim claimed.

Delrahim said the merger would bring more opportunities for writers and directors, as well as actors, drivers, location scouts, casting directors, caterers, mechanics, and animal handlers.

Paramount’s letter pointed to an increase in content production after Paramount merged with Skydance in 2025. Since then, Paramount has either purchased or renewed 20 shows and “will nearly double its theatrical output this year as compared to 2025,” Delrahim wrote.

“More films and series in production means more call sheets, more location days, more transportation, casting, and catering work,” Delrahim wrote.

Paramount’s chief legal officer thinks he knows who's to blame for the company's recent woes with the pending Warner Bros deal: Netflix.

David Ellison's Paramount Skydance deal to take over David Zaslav's Warner Bros Discovery is running into some hurdles as it inches closer to that "ticking fee" deadline, where they have to start paying WBD shareholders for the deal not getting done. Along with concerns from the European Union regarding a monopoly on kids' programming, we also learned that a number of U.S. states are looking to file a lawsuit to block the deal. Earlier today, we learned that Britain's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) had formally opened a probe into the $110 billion deal. The first phase will wrap up on August 7th, at which point the CMA will announce if a second investigation is warranted, which could take months. And then there's the matter of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, which urged the Justice Department back in March to block the deal unless "substantial and enforceable safeguards" were in place to keep jobs secure and promote increased U.S. production. When it comes to that last example, Paramount's chief legal officer Makan Delrahim is pointing a finger directly at… Netflix.

"Netflix's panic-level response and scorched-earth campaign to try and poison regulators and other stakeholders against the Transaction shows just how seriously Netflix takes Paramount as a scaled competitor," Delrahim wrote in a June 5th letter to lawyers in the DOJ's Antitrust Division. Paramount Skydance is arguing that its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery is necessary for it to compete with streaming giants Amazon, Disney and Netflix, and that the mega-deal will bring “new competitive” energy to the entertainment biz.

The argument came in a letter Paramount’s chief legal officer Makan Delrahim sent to California Attorney General Rob Bonta on May 7 “in response to certain misinformation about the marketplace expressed in recent public commentary.”

The letter, which was first reported by Semafor on Tuesday, was sent ahead of a Monday press conference by Bonta in which he left the door open to filing a lawsuit to try to kill the deal.

payload.title: Paramount syyttää Netflixiä vaikuttamiskampanjasta Warner-kauppaa vastaan
payload.summary: Paramount Skydancen lakiasiainjohtaja Makan Delrahim syyttää Netflixiä kampanjasta, jonka tarkoituksena olisi vaikuttaa viranomaisiin ja muihin sidosryhmiin yhtiön suunniteltua Warner Bros. Discoveryn ostoa vastaan.
payload.content:
Paramount Skydance syyttää Netflixiä kampanjasta, jolla se pyrkisi kääntämään Yhdysvaltain kilpailuviranomaisia ja muita sidosryhmiä yhtiön suunniteltua Warner Bros. Discoveryn ostoa vastaan. Väite esitettiin 5. kesäkuuta päivätyssä kirjeessä Yhdysvaltain oikeusministeriön kilpailuosastolle, joka käsittelee media-, viihde- ja viestintäalan kilpailuasioita.

## Kirje osoitettiin kilpailuviranomaisille

Paramountin lakiasiainjohtaja Makan Delrahim osoitti kirjeensä Jared A. Hughesille, joka toimii oikeusministeriön kilpailuosaston Media, Entertainment, and Communications Section -yksikön vt. päällikkönä, sekä kilpailuosaston juristille A. Maya Kahnille. Delrahim on itse aiemmin toiminut kilpailuosaston apulaisoikeusministerinä.

Kirjeessä Delrahim väittää Netflixin yrittäneen vaikuttaa viranomaisiin ja muihin tahoihin, jotta nämä suhtautuisivat kielteisesti Paramountin ja Warner Bros. Discoveryn väliseen yrityskauppaan. Hänen mukaansa Netflixin voimakas reaktio osoittaa, että yhtiö pitää Paramountia merkittävänä kilpailijana, jos kauppa toteutuu.

Paramountin mukaan Netflix on verrannut suunniteltua kauppaa Disneyn ja 21st Century Foxin vuonna 2019 toteutuneeseen yritysjärjestelyyn. Paramount väittää Netflixin käyttäneen vertailua väittääkseen, että vastaavat mediayhtiöiden yhdistymiset voivat vähentää tuotantoa ja kilpailua sekä johtaa irtisanomisiin.

## Teamsters vastusti kauppaa maaliskuussa

Delrahimin kirje on vastaus Teamsters-ammattiliiton maaliskuussa oikeusministeriölle lähettämään kirjeeseen. Liitto katsoi, että Paramountin ja Warner Bros. Discoveryn yhdistyminen voisi uhata elokuva- ja televisioalan työntekijöitä.

Teamsters, jolla on 1,3 miljoonaa jäsentä, pyysi oikeusministeriötä estämään kaupan, ellei siihen liitetä merkittäviä ja toimeenpantavia suojatoimia kotimaisen tuotannon lisäämiseksi ja työpaikkojen turvaamiseksi. Paramount puolestaan kiistää, että kauppa vähentäisi Teamstersin tai muun järjestäytyneen työvoiman työmahdollisuuksia.

Delrahimin mukaan yhdistyminen johtaisi siihen, että Paramount tekisi enemmän sisältöä, mukaan lukien elokuvia sekä suoratoistopalveluille ja televisiokanaville suunnattuja ohjelmia. Hän väittää myös, että lisääntyvä tuotanto painostaisi kilpailijoita toimimaan samoin. Netflixin tai viranomaisten mahdollisista vastauksista kirjeeseen ei ollut aineistossa tietoa.
summary_bullets: Paramount Skydance syyttää Netflixiä vaikuttamisesta suunniteltua Warner Bros. Discovery -kauppaa vastaan.
Väitteet esitettiin 5. kesäkuuta päivätyssä kirjeessä Yhdysvaltain oikeusministeriön kilpailuosastolle.
Teamsters-ammattiliitto on aiemmin vaatinut kaupan estämistä ilman vahvoja työpaikkoja suojaavia ehtoja.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa olleisiin lähdekatkelmiin. Netflixin ja viranomaisten mahdollista vastausta ei ollut aineistossa, joten sitä ei lisätty.
